text:
maria-chen: Heads up — saw a reproducible quality dip after flipping AWQ act-quant to 3 in the canary pool at ~03:10 UTC. ~3-5% drop on our long-context evals (prefix > 1024). short-context tests look fine.
raj-patel: link to the canary dashboard?
infra-bot: canary-deploy: model=custom-14b-raft quant=awq act_bits=3 group_size=128 pool=canary status=successful ts=1765432189
maria-chen: dashboard -> https://internal/redwood/evals/canary/1765432189, check "long-form-qa" suite. notes: token-replacement increases, hallucination up on longer prompts.
jules: ran an offline eval using the same binary and quant flags. reproduce w/ seed=2026. Observed failure mode concentrated when prompt_len > 1024 and when group_size >= 96. with group_size=64 behavior mostly recovered.
sophie: paste of minimal reproduce:
```bash
redwood eval run \\  --model custom-14b-raft \\  --quant awq \\  --group-size 128 \\  --act-bits 3 \\  --suite long-form-qa \\  --seed 2026 \
```
logs show repeated kernel fallback messages: `kernel_select: fallback path kernel_quant_act_small()` and `kv-prefix-mismatch` warnings around generation step ~28.
kevin-l: are we seeing OOMs or numeric saturation? any weird fp exceptions?
jules: no OOMs. numeric saturation hints in the profiler: activation accumulator values spike past int16 range before quantization for certain layers (middle transformer blocks) when prefix has many repeated tokens. looks like act quant scaling may be getting clamped incorrectly for long prefix distributions.
raj-patel: can you try act_bits=4 + group_size=128 to check quality/latency tradeoff?
maria-chen: did that: act_bits=4 brought quality back to within +/-0.5% of baseline on the eval suite, but p95 latency increased ~12ms and token throughput decreased ~6%. quick numbers from canary run:
- baseline fp32: acc=0.874 p95=78ms
- awq act3 g128: acc=0.833 p95=66ms
- awq act4 g128: acc=0.871 p95=78ms
(throughput and mem roughly aligned with latency changes)
sophie: hypothesis: act quant uses a global per-group scale that assumes bounded activation distribution; long prefixes change the activation distribution shape -> scale underestimation -> saturation/clipping -> decode errors. Two mitigations: increase act_bits for suspect layers, or make group sizing dynamic by effective prefix length.
kevin-l: can we implement a quick per-request override: if prefix_len > 1024 then fallback act_bits=4? low-effort and targeted.
jules: quick config prototype:
```json
{
  "quant_profile":"awq",
  "act_bits":{"default":3, "overrides":[{"min_prefix":1024, "bits":4}]},
  "group_size_policy":"prefix-aware"
}
```
(just a config blob, not yet wire-up)
raj-patel: we should also test per-layer top-k fallback: bump bits for mid-blocks 10..22 and keep others at 3. cheaper than global 4.
sophie: ran a micro-batch with per-layer fallback on a dev box. result: quality recovered to baseline, p95 +6ms vs act3 global. profiler trace attached: `profiler://trace/1765432235` (internal). key lines: `layer 14 pre-quant scale=0.00012 -> post clamp=0.00002` repeated 7x.
infra-bot: autoscaler: noted group-size oscillation in canary at 03:11-03:14 due to bursty tail; rotated 2 nodes out.
ci-bot: rollouts/freeze: placed canary on hold until root-cause analysis completed by eng-ml.
maria-chen: immediate plan: 1) revert act_bits to 4 for canary (mitigates quality), 2) run targeted A/B with per-layer fallback on 10% traffic, 3) add prefix-aware policy to runtime to choose group_size <=64 for prefix>2048 and <=128 otherwise.
jules: longer-term: improve scale estimation in AWQ pre-pass (track more robust moments) or add dynamic clip head. I'll draft a tech note and perf/quality reg test.
raj-patel: assign tickets: ENG-ML-4521 (revert + AB), ENG-ML-4522 (per-layer fallback), ENG-ML-4523 (prefix-aware group policy).
maria-chen: thanks — I'll follow up with data and the canary logs. tagging @sophie @jules for the perf traces. :thumbsup:
